name: @media-router/plugin-mpegts-muxer
description: MPEG-TS muxer — combines any number of MPEG-TS sources (video, audio, subtitles) into a single transport stream

mediaRouter.description: Combines several muxed/mpegts streams into one — any input takes any stream type (video, audio, KLV/WebVTT or DVB subtitles).

inputs.description: Inputs — "+ Add" creates another input port. Any input takes any MPEG-TS source: every stream it carries (video, audio, KLV/WebVTT subtitles, DVB or teletext subtitles) is re-muxed onto its own fixed PID — automatic by input index, or set per stream below. Give an input a language and it is written into the output PMT as its streams' ISO 639 language descriptor — the standard signalling a downstream splitter labels from ("Audio nor").

name.description: Label for this input pin in the editor (optional). Not carried in the transport stream — MPEG-TS has no standard stream-name field; use Language for signalling receivers understand.

language.description: ISO 639 language code (2/3-letter, e.g. en / eng / deu) written into the output PMT as the language descriptor of this input's streams — the standard signalling every receiver understands (audio today; KLV/teletext once mpegtsmux carries it for them). Blank passes the source stream's own language through unchanged. Applied at pipeline build — changing it restarts the muxer.

offsetMs.description: Lipsync offset for this input's AUDIO stream on the mux timeline. Negative advances audio — set to minus the measured audio-late skew to cancel a stable path delay with no added latency (costs ~|offset| of clipped audio at pipeline start). Re-measure after changing audio-path buffering. Applied at pad-link time — changing it restarts the muxer.

pid.description: Output PID of this input's video; its other streams follow — audio +1, KLV/WebVTT subtitles +2, DVB/teletext subtitles +3. Leave 0 to assign automatically (input 1 → 256, input 2 → 264, …): the assigned value is written back here so the field shows the PID in use. A block overlapping another input's, or touching 4096 (PMT), stops the muxer with an error naming the clash. Changing it restarts the muxer.

alignment.description: MPEG-TS muxer alignment — keep at SRT-aligned for SRT/RIST/UDP transport. Use Continuous only for v1-style receivers that derive timing from byte flow (their tsparse mis-estimates bitrate from 1316 B bursts)

queueLeaky.description: Input queue behaviour. OFF (non-leaky): never drop — hold the leading stream up to Queue depth while waiting out A/V skew or a stall; backlog flushes after recovery (contribution/stability). ON (leaky): shed the oldest frame once Queue depth of backlog builds, so output resumes at the live edge immediately after a stall (live production). Queues sit upstream of the muxer, after the codec parser — drops always land on whole frames; the mux output itself is never queued (a drop there would corrupt the TS mid-frame).

videoParserBypass.description: Low-latency video input: skip the H.264/H.265 parser in front of the mux and take each demuxed access unit as-is. Saves one frame of latency per video input (40 ms at 25 fps) — the parser can only close a frame when the next one starts. Only for sources that repeat SPS/PPS before every keyframe (every Media Router encoder does); on a foreign source with sloppy PES framing leave this OFF, the parser is what re-frames it and speeds recovery after packet loss. Applied at pad-link time — changing it restarts the muxer.

queueDepthMs.description: Input queue bound. Non-leaky: how much A/V arrival skew to absorb without back-pressuring (set ≥ the worst skew of your wiring: transcode chain ~200 ms, demuxer audio pacing 160 ms, B-frame delay ~120 ms). Leaky: how much backlog to tolerate before shedding starts.
